discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly Tel Aviv University)

subfield: Condensed matter physics (2D materials, strongly correlated electrons)
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted, with a simple continuum model, that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees the Dirac velocity of bilayer graphene vanishes and nearly flat moire bands emerge. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realised this regime experimentally, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity whose phase diagram recalls that of the cuprates. Together these works founded 'twistronics': the twist angle became a new control knob that turns a weakly interacting semimetal into a tunable strongly correlated system. The field has since revealed orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, fractional Chern insulators and correlated physics in many moire materials. This is a rare case of a clean theoretical prediction followed by a decisive experiment that opened a whole new area of quantum-matter research, on a platform where interactions, topology and band structure can be tuned in one device.
